title: Contains Duplicate
summary: You get a list of integers `nums` in no particular order. Decide whether any value appears more than once in it: return `true` if some value repeats, and `false` if every value is different. The copies of a repeated value can sit anywhere in the list, not only side by side.

examples.explanation: 1 appears at index 1 and again at index 4, with other values in between.

approaches.twist: Keep a set of the numbers seen so far, and return true as soon as a number is already in it.
Compare every pair of numbers, and return true when two of them are equal.
approaches.note: Works with O(1) extra space, but comparing every pair takes O(n²) time. The target is O(n).

approaches.twist: Sort the numbers so equal values end up side by side, then compare each number with the next one.
approaches.note: Works with little extra space if you sort in place, but sorting takes O(n log n) time. The target is O(n).

signals.meaning: A repeat is a value you have already met. Keep the values you pass in a set, and check each new one against it before adding it.
Copies can sit far apart, so comparing neighbors misses them unless you sort first, which costs O(n log n). A set of the values seen so far catches a repeat wherever it is.
All different means a set of the values is exactly as long as the list, so comparing len(set(nums)) with len(nums) settles it too.

constraintReading: len(nums) can reach 10⁵, so comparing every pair means about 5·10⁹ checks: O(n²) is far too slow. Sorting first brings it down to O(n log n). The O(n) time target asks for one pass with O(1) set lookups, paid for with O(n) space.

hints.clarify: Do the two copies have to sit next to each other? No: they can be anywhere. Try [4, 9, 2, 9, 7] by hand: 9 shows up at index 1 and again at index 3, so the answer is true even though a 2 sits between them. And a list with a single value can never hold a repeat.
hints.approach: Hash set of the values seen so far. Walk through `nums` once. Before you add a value to the set, check whether it is already there: if it is, you met it earlier, so a value repeats and you can stop with true. If the walk ends without a hit, every value was new, so return false.
hints.whyNot: Comparing every pair of values works, but it is O(n²): about 5·10⁹ comparisons for 10⁵ numbers. Sorting puts equal values side by side, so a single pass over neighbors finds a repeat, but the sort costs O(n log n). A set checks membership in O(1), so one pass is enough.

slots.setup: An empty set `seen`. It holds every value you have passed so far; you only need to know whether a value was there, not where.
slots.loop: Visit `nums` once, from left to right, one value `x` at a time.
slots.update: When `x` is not in `seen` yet, add it, so a later copy can find it.
slots.record: Before adding `x`, look it up in `seen`. A hit means `x` appeared earlier: you've found a repeat.
slots.return: Return true as soon as a lookup hits. If the loop ends with no hit, every value was different, so return false.

solution.explanation: The loop visits each value once, and each set lookup and insert takes O(1) time on average, so the time is O(n). When no value repeats, every value ends up in `seen`, so the space is O(n). `len(set(nums)) < len(nums)` gives the same answer in one line, but it always builds the whole set, even when the repeat sits at the very start.

events.label: look up
events.say: nums[{i}] is {x}. Is {x} already in seen?

events.label: store
events.say: {x} isn't in seen, so this is its first appearance. Add it to seen

events.label: repeat
events.say: {x} is already in seen: it appeared earlier, so a value repeats. Return true

events.label: return
events.say: Every value was new when it arrived, so nothing repeats. Return false

predict.ask: Is this value already in seen?
Will the next value be a repeat?
predict.answerWhen: i + 1 < len(nums) and (nums[i + 1] in seen or nums[i + 1] == x)

related.relation: Same one pass with a memory of the values so far, but each number looks up the partner it needs instead of a copy of itself.
Also spots a repeat with a set of what it has seen, but only inside a window that slides forward.
